ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Sick Visit — Benjamin Franklin — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for a hot, swollen left knee

text.paragraph: Hot, swollen left knee for two days. [S]

Mr. Franklin is a 76-year-old man with gout, stage 3a chronic kidney disease, and hypertension, seven weeks after his allopurinol was increased to 300 mg daily, who asked for a same-day visit. Two days ago, the morning after a long dinner with wine and roast meats, he woke with pain in the left knee, which has become hot and swollen and too painful to bend. He has never had gout in the knee; his earlier flares were in the right big toe. He takes colchicine 0.6 mg daily and has not missed doses. He has felt warm but has had no chills. He has had no injury, skin break, or recent procedure other than his prostate operation eleven weeks ago, and no urinary symptoms. He has taken acetaminophen, which barely helps, and no ibuprofen, as his kidney plan advises. [S]

list.item:
Acute gout flare of the left knee (M10.062). Aspiration shows urate crystals and a negative Gram stain, which confirms gout. Infection is not suspected, but culture is pending because septic arthritis can coexist with crystals. Flares are common in the first months of urate lowering; this one followed a rich meal with wine. Serum urate today is 5.9 mg/dL, but levels can read falsely low during a flare. [S]
Prednisone 40 mg each morning with food for 5 days.
Continue allopurinol 300 mg and colchicine 0.6 mg daily; do not stop allopurinol during a flare.
Ice, rest, and elevation; no NSAIDs because of chronic kidney disease.
Call the same day if fever, chills, or spreading redness develop; we will call with the culture result.

Chronic kidney disease stage G3a (N18.31). Creatinine 1.33 mg/dL, eGFR 55, stable. Potassium 4.7 mmol/L on losartan and potassium citrate, seven weeks after starting potassium citrate. [S]
Continue losartan and potassium citrate.

Hypertension (I10). Blood pressure 136/80 mmHg, raised by pain. [S]
Recheck at the next review.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: 2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout (2020); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and benign prostatic hyperplasia monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Telephone call with the culture result in two days. Gout, kidney, and blood pressure review in September with a serum urate when he is free of the flare. Next scheduled visit 1782-09-14: gout, stone prevention, kidney, and blood pressure review at about six months. [S]
